story.who: Maxwell Alexandre is a painter whose work has drawn attention abroad, according to the website of the gallery Almeida & Dale, for two series: Pardo é Papel, about everyday scenes in a favela, and Novo Poder, about black people in places of power.
story.now: The show shares its title with Alexandre's first solo exhibition at Almeida & Dale, which the gallery's website says draws on two sets of works, Clube and Cubo Branco. Clube began in 2020, when he started visiting a club in Gávea, and he then turned to painting white bodies, a change from earlier work that had shown only black people. Almeida & Dale says "white figuration" is his way of making whiteness visible in painting and art history.

evidence.quote:
Maxwell Alexandre
Black painter, white figuration
9 Oct – 28 Nov 2026

He has garnered international recognition for his Pardo é Papel (Brown is Paper) and Novo Poder (New Power) series, respectively portraying day-to-day scenes in the favela and black people in spaces of power.
Maxwell Alexandre completely transforms the space at Almeida & Dale Fradique in pintor preto, figuração branca. (Black painter, white figuration), his first solo show at the gallery.
The Clube (Club) series was initiated in 2020, when Maxwell started going to Clube de Regatas do Flamengo in Gávea
Maxwell turned his attention to white bodies, a turning point in his career — hitherto marked by the exclusive portrayal of black people —
the pictorial genre of “white figuration” becomes a conceptual operation to highlight whiteness in the field of painting and in art history
two iconic sets of artworks: Clube (Club), first shown at the Rio de Janeiro Historical Museum (2024), and Cubo Branco (White Cube)
